newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets studying rise in Dutch swine fever.
newsitem.headline: EU vets studying rise in Dutch swine fever.

text.p: The European Union is seeking an explanation for increasing cases of swine fever in the Netherlands despite tough controls in place since January, an EU member state official said on Monday.
"The eradication and movement controls which were approved by the European Commission should have diminished the number of cases but there has in fact been an increase," the official said.

On Friday a special meeting of the EU's standing veterinary committee closed the whole of the Netherlands for trade in pigmeat and pig semen because of swine fever which first broke out at the end of January.
The EU closed off most trade from the Netherlands in January because of the disease, which was later traced to Paderborn, Germany.
Veterinary experts are now seeking an explanation for the small increase in the number of outbreaks.
"There are some problems because the incidence is not diminishing but is increasing a little bit.
"The measures taken in the Netherlands were approved by the Commission and experts are now looking for an explanaton," the official added.
